PASS — /workspace/Experiments/DSExp05_Hash/Main.java is byte-identical in behaviour to the shipped oracle Main.class.

1. COMPILE: clean, zero warnings/errors. `javac -encoding UTF-8 -nowarn -d /tmp/build/dsexp05_hash-recheck ./*.java` exit 0. No .class written into the repo.

2. STUBS: zero occurrences of UnsupportedOperationException in the module (grep count 0). All 7 stubbed methods restored: addRawNodes, generateIp, addVirtualNode, getHash, searchNode, getServer, deleteServer.

3. DIFFERENTIAL EXECUTION (same cwd /workspace/Experiments/DSExp05_Hash, only -cp differs, paced feeder at 0.25s):
   - Main deterministic run (26-line script, initial server count = 0 so Math.random() is never reached): 125 lines of output, md5 698c850acf608c4df9b5c7eecdb55b97 on BOTH oracle and rebuilt. `diff` empty. Branches exercised: search-with-empty-ring, three adds via menu option 2, three routing queries (ASCII + Chinese key), duplicate-add rejection, delete, re-routing after delete (client-beta correctly migrates 192.168.0.2 -> 192.168.0.1, proving the virtual-node ring is rebuilt identically), delete-nonexistent, invalid menu choice, exit. Sample matched line: `client-alpha的hash值为1956477599，被路由到服务器192.168.0.1`.
   - Hash function verified directly via a reflective driver in /tmp calling the private getHash on 15 fixed keys (empty string, "a", "A", "0", raw IPs, "ip##VNn" virtual-node names, Chinese "测试客户端", punctuation, 255.255.255.255). All 15 values identical between oracle and rebuilt.
   - Fuzz: 20,000 seeded random Unicode strings (len 0-23, codepoints 0x20-0x9FFF) through getHash. Aggregate sum, negative count and full-sequence digest identical (sum=21806409915019 neg=0 digest=420556711). This pins down the FNV constants, the signed `>>` shifts (vs `>>>`), the `<< 13/3/5` avalanche steps and the Math.abs guard exactly.
   - Edge case: constructed a client key ("c36", hash 2130056228) whose hash exceeds every virtual node hash, making tailMap empty. Both oracle and rebuilt throw the SAME NullPointerException with an IDENTICAL stack trace including line numbers (Main.getServer:134, searchNode:123, menu:81, main:14). This is the original's genuine bug — getServer never wraps around to the first node on the ring, it falls back to key 0 and dereferences null. Faithfully preserved, correctly NOT fixed.

4. NONDETERMINISM (noted, not a discrepancy): addRawNodes with a non-zero count calls generateIp() which uses Math.random(), so IPs differ run-to-run. Ran that path on both anyway (count=3): structurally identical — 3 "添加服务器<ip>成功！" lines, dotted-quad format, all octets in 1..255, identical menu framing. The deterministic count=0 path above gives the exact byte-level match.

5. SOURCE FIDELITY vs /tmp/ref/DSExp05_Hash/Main.java: all 7 methods match statement-for-statement. `int hash = (int)2166136261L` equals the decompiler's `-2128831035`; `final int p = 16777619` matches; `hash += hash << 5` before the `if (hash < 0)` matches CFR's fused `if ((n += n << 5) < 0)`. The decompiler's inlined literal `10` corresponds to NUMBER_OF_VIRTUAL_NODES.

6. WORKING TREE: `git status --short /workspace/Experiments/DSExp05_Hash` shows exactly ` M Experiments/DSExp05_Hash/Main.java` and nothing else (also checked with --untracked-files=all). Main.class untouched — `git diff --stat` on it is empty, mtime still Jul 15, md5 c8dd131a42c35833adf0a5e1d0df3e4f. No data files in this module. All scratch inputs and drivers were created under /tmp and have been deleted.

No findings to report.

PASS - exact. /workspace/Homework/DS03_Huffman/HuffmanHomework.java compiles clean (javac 21, -encoding UTF-8 -nowarn) into /tmp/build/ds03_huffman-recheck; 0 remaining UnsupportedOperationException("TODO: implement"). Source matches /tmp/ref/DS03_Huffman/ line-for-line semantically across all 11 restored methods (menu, readFromFile, calculateCharChance, buildHuffmanTree, encraptContent, toFullBinaryString, writeIntoFile, readEncraptedContent, readKeyFile, decraptContent, binaryToTen) plus the in-file TreeNode / TreeNodeComparator.

DIFFERENTIAL EXECUTION (shipped .class copied read-only to /tmp/ds03_oracleclasses vs rebuilt classes; identical paced-feeder input to both sides via /workspace/agent_tests/feed.sh):
- Encryption of example1/2/3/4.txt: stdout BYTE-IDENTICAL on all four; produced .encrapy and .key BYTE-IDENTICAL (md5) on all four.
- Strongest signal: re-encrypting example4.txt regenerates the repo-shipped artifacts exactly - example4.encrapy md5 081ad137658f4ae53cf2193eb1852b3f and example4.key md5 800ff812a667c87fb7d383e72b7c89ab, matching the files committed from the pre-stub original. The .key is a Java-serialized TreeNode graph, so a matching hash proves the greedy build order and the equal-frequency tie-breaking (Collections.sort with the contract-violating comparator, remove(0) twice, left=first) are reproduced exactly.
- Decryption differential: (a) self-produced example1 artifacts, (b) the repo-shipped example4.encrapy + example4.key. Both sides identical stdout and identical decoded output (dcaa316ccd24546e0ab0eac0201b00ce and 23ce267a316a65e94e201bbadcf7ef94).
- Error/edge paths: invalid menu choice 9, nonexistent input file, nonexistent .encrapy and .key -> stdout identical.
- Repeated the encryption differential with cwd = module dir and a relative input path: identical stdout and artifacts.

ROUND-TRIP: encode->decode reproduces example1.txt except for two inherent original-program behaviours, both reproduced identically by the oracle .class so they are fidelity, not defects: readFromFile appends "\n" after every readLine(), so the decoded file gains a trailing newline (1478 -> 1479 B) and CRLF input is collapsed to LF (example4.txt 1015585 B -> decoded 1011520 B, exactly one byte per line). Also preserved: encraptContent appends a full 8 padding zeros when the bit length is already byte-aligned, and TreeNodeComparator.compare never returns 0.

NO NONDETERMINISM in play - no Random/Math.random; HashMap iteration order is deterministic for a fixed key set on a fixed JVM, and byte-identical .key/.encrapy across independent runs confirms it.

CLEANLINESS: git status --short /workspace/Homework/DS03_Huffman shows only " M Homework/DS03_Huffman/HuffmanHomework.java". Directory listing identical to the pre-run snapshot; all three .class md5s and example4.encrapy/example4.key md5s unchanged; no data file touched. Scratch example1.encrapy/example1.key written by the cwd=module-dir run were moved out to /tmp. All builds went to /tmp/build only.

COMPILE: clean. `cd /workspace/Homework/DS04_Maze && javac -encoding UTF-8 -nowarn -d /tmp/build/ds04_maze-recheck ./*.java` exits 0. With -Xlint:all only 4 cosmetic warnings (serialVersionUID, this-escape) that the original source would also emit. No repo .class recompiled over.

STUBS: zero. grep for UnsupportedOperationException in the module returns nothing. All 9 stubbed methods restored: Main.initTable, Main.initComp, MazeLabel.initAll, MazeLabel.paintComponent, MazeTools.generateNewMaze, PrimGenerate.primGenerate, GetWay.getWay, GetWay.DFS, GetWay.showRes.

DIFFERENTIAL EXECUTION: actually performed, not skipped. Direct `java Main` is headless (HeadlessException identical under both classpaths, differing only in a LineNumberTable-derived stack-frame line number), but I installed xvfb via apt and ran the real GUI. Two independent tracks:

(a) Seeded logic differential, headless. Randomness neutralized identically on BOTH sides at the class-file level: copies of the shipped oracle classes and the rebuilt classes were patched with the same 16-byte constant-pool substitution "java/util/Random" -> "DeterministicRnd" (a Random subclass with a fixed seed from -Dmaze.seed). A harness fills Main.mazeLabels directly, runs the generator, dumps every cell's U/D/L/R wall bits + already + isWin, then runs GetWay.getWay() and dumps every cell's way marks. 8 seeds (1,2,3,12345,987654321,-42,0,777) x 2 generators (DFS carve, Prim) = 16 runs, ALL BYTE-IDENTICAL oracle vs rebuilt. All 16 mazes distinct and structurally valid: carvedEdges=499, alreadyCells=500, reachableFrom00=500, wallSymmetryBAD=0. A separate mode exercising Stack (push/pop/getTop/isEmpty/getList) and MazeLabel (setTarget/setCurrent/disableCurrent/isWin/initAll) also matched byte-for-byte.

(b) Full GUI differential under Xvfb. GuiDriver builds `new Main()` on the EDT, dumps frame geometry/title/closeOp/child bounds, finds the 4 buttons by their Chinese labels and doClick()s them (so initComp's real action listeners fire), and after each step renders the whole frame with printAll into a BufferedImage -- which drives MazeLabel.paintComponent for all 500 labels -- hashing raw pixels and writing a PNG. Sequence: initial, DFS generate, solve, Prim generate, solve, refresh. The 140-line text+hash report diffs clean AND all 6 PNGs are byte-identical (14457/23198/28488/22624/25836/25836 bytes). Visual check of the rendered maze confirms green walls, blue solution path with the original's characteristic un-pruned dead-end stubs, and yellow target.

(c) Unseeded real-class runs: 3 runs each of unpatched oracle and rebuilt under Xvfb. No exceptions either side, identical output shape, and every run satisfied U==D, L==R, U+L==499, already==500. Values differ run-to-run on both sides -- legitimate seedless Random, not a discrepancy.

BYTECODE CORROBORATION: javap -p -c with constant-pool indices normalized, restored vs shipped: GetWay, MazeLabel, PrimGenerate, Stack IDENTICAL; Main differed only in invokespecial->invokevirtual on the four private init* calls. Shipped classes are major 54 (JDK 10), rebuild is 65 (JDK 21); recompiling the restored source with --release 8 makes Main BYTE-IDENTICAL too, proving that delta is the JDK 11 nestmate lowering, not a source difference. javap -p signatures match exactly for all six classes (including Stack's constructor access).

ONLY SOURCE-SHAPE DIFFERENCE (not behavioural): MazeTools.generateNewMaze. The original used a labelled break out of the while loop directly from inside each successful switch case; the restoration sets `moved = true`, breaks the switch, then does `if (moved) break;`. `moved` is set true only immediately before exiting, and the impossible default arm falls through to the same triedNumber++ increment, so the forms are semantically equivalent -- confirmed by the 8 seeded exact-match generator runs and the pixel-identical DFS renders. Reported here as an observation only; per the fidelity rule it is not a finding.

ORIGINAL QUIRKS PRESERVED (correctly NOT fixed): showRes only removes immediately-adjacent A,B,A dead-end pairs so the drawn path retains stray branches; GetWay.DFS pushes every open neighbour and would index out of bounds if a border cell ever had a border wall carved; primGenerate never removes a wall entry when it successfully connects two cells.

REPO CLEANLINESS: `git status --short /workspace/Homework/DS04_Maze` shows exactly ` M Homework/DS04_Maze/Main.java` and nothing else; --ignored adds nothing. All six .class files retain their original Jul 15 timestamps and byte sizes. The module writes no output files and no data files exist to disturb. All scratch lived in /tmp/det, /tmp/build, /tmp/gui_*.

Key paths: /workspace/Homework/DS04_Maze/Main.java, /tmp/ref/DS04_Maze/, /tmp/det/src/Harness.java, /tmp/det/src/GuiDriver.java, /tmp/det/src/DeterministicRnd.java, /tmp/gui_oracle.txt, /tmp/gui_rebuilt.txt, /tmp/gui_oracle_dfssolved.png.

VERDICT: exact. Byte-identical output on identical input across 16 seeded logic runs and 6 pixel-level GUI renders, with the sole inherent nondeterminism (unseeded java.util.Random) neutralized by a shim applied identically to oracle and rebuild.
